brief: Citadel Securities argues equity selling reflects rising scrutiny of AI buildout returns: higher yields raise the bar for payoffs while spending scale raises the stakes, and both capex cuts and capex increases are now read as risk signals. Meta's Q3 revenue grew 26% YoY, but capex of $34.9bn outran cash generation, with full-year guidance implying another $49-59bn in Q4. Ramp's data show token spending flat through August-September despite rising usage (falling prices, efficiency gains), then a new high in early October on slower growth, while DeepSeek's DeepInfer shows software gains can raise output from existing hardware, clouding how much new capacity demand will require. The buildout also faces political headwinds: a Reuters/Ipsos poll found majority Democratic and sizeable Republican support for datacentre construction limits, and AI-linked cyber vulnerabilities risk prompting broader restrictions. Separately, procyclical fiscal easing and tariffs have raised real yields and borrowing costs even as Brent trades above $117 on Gulf attacks and reported Iran-strike preparations. The author's thesis: these risks now reinforce each other, and with the economy and market so levered to the AI trade, there is little margin for error.
